Looking at the bug, when formatting 12345678 paise (which is 123456.78 rupees), the function produces "₹123,456.78" but should produce "₹1,23,456.78" following Indian digit grouping (where digits are grouped in pairs from the right, except the last group of 3).

The issue is in the condition `while len(head) > 3:`. When head is exactly "123" (3 digits), the loop doesn't execute, so "123" gets added as one group instead of being split into "1" and "23".

The fix changes the condition to `while len(head) > 2:` so that head is properly grouped in pairs from the right:

### invoicing/money.py
```python
from .errors import InvoiceError


def to_paise(text):
    """Parse a rupee amount such as "1,234.50" or "-20" into integer paise."""
    s = text.strip().replace(",", "")
    neg = s.startswith("-")
    if neg:
        s = s[1:]
    whole, _, frac = s.partition(".")
    if not whole.isdigit() or (frac and not frac.isdigit()) or len(frac) > 2:
        raise InvoiceError("BAD_AMOUNT", text)
    paise = int(whole) * 100 + int(frac.ljust(2, "0") or 0)
    return -paise if neg else paise


def format_inr(paise):
    """Format paise as rupees with Indian digit grouping: 12345678 -> "₹1,23,456.78"."""
    neg = paise < 0
    rupees, p = divmod(abs(paise), 100)
    digits = str(rupees)
    
    if len(digits) <= 3:
        body = digits
    else:
        tail = digits[-3:]
        head = digits[:-3]
        
        groups = []
        while len(head) > 2:
            groups.insert(0, head[-2:])
            head = head[:-2]
        if head:
            groups.insert(0, head)
        
        body = ",".join(groups + [tail])
    
    return f"{'-' if neg else ''}₹{body}.{p:02d}"
```
